title: Implant-free loop tenodesis compared to arthroscopic anchor tenodesis for treatment of the long head of biceps: a multi-center non-inferiority randomized controlled trial
summary:
Minimally invasive video-assisted shoulder surgery by so called arthroscopy is the fourth most performed surgery by orthopedic surgeons and among the 20 most performed surgeries at all. In over 75% of these surgeries, disorders of the tendon of the long head of the two-headed biceps muscle can be found, which require treatment. This long tendon of biceps muscle is frequently responsible for shoulder pain in the adult population across all age groups; When mechanical load has damaged the tendon, the standard treatment is to remove the tendon from its origin and reattach it to the bone outside the mechanically stressed area. This technique is called “tenodesis”. For safe reattachment of the tendon, established techniques use some sort of screw or bone implant. However, several adverse events have been reported after using these implant materials including implant tear out, wound infections, continuing shoulder pain, and shoulder fractures. To avoid these risks, a new easy to learn and fast to perform surgical technique was developed by Kerschbaum in 2019, which provides stable attachment of the tendon to the bone without the need for an implant. The new procedure is meant to combine safe attachment of the tendon with fewer complications compared to established procedures. In a laboratory testing, the so called “loop tenodesis” procedure has demonstrated stable fixation of the tendon. A first survey observing 50 patients after receiving the new surgical procedure has shown good short and medium term results. Therefore, we plan to compare patient-reported results after the new “loop tenodesis” to that after the existing standard therapy in a patient-blinded trial. Treatment of study patients will take place at five German treating centers. Both the control intervention and the experimental intervention are already routinely performed surgical techniques at all of the participating centers. All patients that require surgical treatment at the participating centers because of problems caused by changes
of the long tendon of the biceps muscle will be considered suitable for study participation. All participating patients will be informed about the study and the procedures applied and only after proclamation of their written consent are randomly treated by one of two surgical techniques without being told their received treatment method. All patients will be examined at regular intervals over a period of 2 years following surgery. We expect the new loop tenodesis technique to provide postoperative results that are equal to those of implant-based techniques, while leading to fewer complications. The study could help to establish a new standard treatment in shoulder surgery reducing perioperative complications.
conditions: Injury of muscle and tendon of long head of biceps

interventions.name: Arthroscopic implant-free loop tenodesis of the long head of biceps  (experimental intervention group)
Arthroscopic epiosseous anchor tenodesis of the long head of biceps (standard-of-care intervention group)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Written informed consent

At least one of the following: 
- partial or subtotal tears of the LHB tendon,
- chronic LHB inflammation,
- LHB instability (pulley lesions) 
- traumatic or degenerative SLAP lesions
Exclusion criteria:
- osteoarthritis of the affected or contralateral shoulder 
- shoulder stiffness, 
- chronic glenohumeral instability
- (previous) distal biceps tendon lesions 
- previous surgery on the contralateral shoulder
- concomitant fracture of the shoulders/arms
- concomitant neurovascular injury of the affected shoulder/arm
- intake of oral corticosteroids
- age under 18 years or other reasons for lacking capability to consent
